messages.author: 207205de2f4712d1
messages.subject: I updated to the latest version of shiny... an error now occurs... also: reactiveValues()
parts:
Thank you for shiny!

I have just installed the latest version of shiny, after having developed a relatively extensive app... and I now get this error. I'm not sure *exactly* what shiny is trying to tell me. Prior to updating shiny, the app ran very smoothly... update... error... ???

> runApp()

Listening on port 8100
Error in envRefInferField(x, what, getClass(class(x)), selfEnv) : 
  ‘request’ is not a valid field or method name for reference class “WebSocket”


I have another question also:

if server.R look like this:

vars <- reactiveValues()
vars[['user_data']] <- data.frame()
shinyServer(function(input, output)) {
  observe({
    input$actionbutton
    vars[['user_data']] <- rbind(vars[['user_data']], data.frame(a = 1, b = 2))
  })
}

... with an actionButton('actionbutton', 'click me') in the ui.R file... is the 'vars' object unique to each visitor who loads the page, or is 'vars' (because it's on the server-side) something that all users would be manipulating any time anybody clicks the same actionButton? (which would be quite chaotic) ... I've been using these reactiveValues() for a bit now, but am unsure how shiny will respond when multiple people are using it at the same time.

The tutorial says, "The values in input are set by input from the web browser." - not trying to be finicky, but can you elaborate a little on reactive values. Or, if you know where a good discussion thread is, that would helps also. I found some talk about it, but couldn't find an answer for my situation.

Thank you!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: I updated to the latest version of shiny... an error now occurs... also: reactiveValues()
parts:
What version of httpuv do you have installed?

For your second question, it depends entirely on how visible the "vars" variable is. If it's declared inside your shinyServer function, then it's unique to each session. If it's declared in global.R or the top of server.R, then it's shared by all sessions, and reactivity caused by one session will trigger changes in any other sessions that have a reactive dependency on it. See this article: http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping

Note that these are all supported uses of reactivity; there's nothing wrong with having reactivity flow across sessions if that's what you want.

Because the "input" object is passed into your shinyServer function, it's specific to each session; a unique input and output object is created at the start of each session.

Does that answer your question?

parts:
Yes it does. I hadn't considered defining reactiveValues() inside of the shinyServer() function, but that is exactly what I want - thank you!

I ran install.packages('httpuv') and now things seem to be working properly. Thank you for your time, and quick response.

Are there any discussions or documents about what to expect from the enterprise edition of shiny server? ... I recently read that a release date is still not decided on - is this still the case? ... specifically, I could use authentication, but that's the only thing I think of when I think about the enterprise edition.

Thanks again. Since the day I learned R I've desired [shiny], and I'm loving this pacakge!

Dan
